summary: Aligned redirect analytics with the Module 3 contract, reproduced the concurrency race under load, then fixed it with an atomic Postgres upsert and re-verified with the same reproduction script.
evidence: Reproduction conditions were held constant at 30 concurrent requests across 5 rounds.
Pre-fix run on check-then-insert path returned a 500 response in round 1 (status counts included {"307":29,"500":1}) and ended with 'BUG REPRODUCED: observed HTTP 500 under concurrent load.'
Server logs during pre-fix run showed 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "analytics_link_id_bucket_unique"' (UniqueViolation), confirming the race on (link_id, timestamp_bucket).
Applied fix by replacing check-then-insert with one atomic SQL statement: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (link_id, timestamp_bucket) DO UPDATE SET count = analytics.count + 1, last_accessed_at = NOW().
Post-fix run with the identical 30x5 workload returned only 307 responses in every round and ended with 'NO REPRO: no HTTP 500 observed under current test conditions.'
Post-fix log scan found no UniqueViolation entries.
